1. What is the difference between a data warehouse and a data lake?

A data warehouse is a structured repository of data that is used for reporting and analysis. It is designed to support the efficient querying and analysis of large amounts of data, and is typically used to support business intelligence and data analysis activities.

A data lake, on the other hand, is a more flexible and unstructured repository of data that can store a wide variety of data types and formats. It is designed to support the storage and analysis of large amounts of data, and is often used to support big data and machine learning activities.

One key difference between a data warehouse and a data lake is their approach to data structure. A data warehouse is typically designed with a well-defined schema that specifies the structure and relationships of the data, while a data lake is designed to be more flexible and allow for a wider range of data types and formats.

Another key difference is their use case. A data warehouse is typically used for reporting and analysis, while a data lake is often used for big data and machine learning activities.

In summary, a data warehouse is a structured repository of data designed for reporting and analysis, while a data lake is a more flexible and unstructured repository of data designed for the storage and analysis of large amounts of data.

Notable characteristics may include futuristic settings, advanced technology, and imaginative storylines.
7. Thriller:

These genres often include elements of suspense, danger, and mystery, with a focus on tense and suspenseful storylines. Notable characteristics may include suspenseful storylines, high-stakes conflicts, and tense atmospheres.

要在 LaTeX 文檔中自動生成表格，您可以使用 `acronym` 和 `glossaries` 套件。以下是一個示例，展示了如何在 LaTeX 文檔中使用這些套件來生成表格。

首先，我們需要安裝 `acronym` 和 `glossaries` 套件。您可以使用 `texlive-full` 或 `miktex` 等軟件包管理器來安裝這些套件。

1. 在 LaTeX 文件的開頭添加以下命令，以引入 `acronym` 和 `glossaries` 套件：
```
\usepackage{acronym}
\usepackage{glossaries}
```
2. 在文檔的開頭，使用 `\makeglossaries` 命令來建立詞彙表。這將在文檔結尾生成一個 `.gls` 檔案，其中包含所有的詞彙。
```
\begin{document}

% 在這裡放置您的文本

\makeglossaries

% 在這裡放置您的文本

\printglossary[type=\acronymtype]

\end{document}
```
3. 在文檔的結尾，使用 `\newacro` 命令來定義新的詞彙。例如，以下命令定義了一個新的詞彙 `myacro`：
```
\newacro{myacro}{My Acronym}
```
4. 在文檔中使用 `\ac` 命令來引用新的詞彙。例如，以下命令使用 `myacro` 詞彙：
```
\ac{myacro}
```
5. 最後，使用 `\printglossary` 命令來將詞彙表導出到文檔中。這將在文檔結尾生成一個表格，其中包含所有的詞彙。
```
\printglossary[type=\acronymtype]
```

以上是一個簡單的示例，展示了如何使用 `acronym` 和 `glossaries` 套件來自動生成表格。您可以根據您的需求進一步自定義詞彙和表格。

context: Ten European football teams – the Netherlands, England, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and Wales – will participate in a season-long “OneLove” campaign promoting inclusion and opposing discrimination.
expected_response:
Every country except Sweden and Norway has qualified for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and each captain of these eight nations will wear a distinctive OneLove armband – which features a heart containing colors from all backgrounds – during the tournament.
The Netherlands FA, which is spearheading the campaign, chose the colors to represent all heritages, backgrounds, genders and sexual identities; the armband will be worn in Qatar where same-sex relationships are a criminal offense.
Sweden and Norway will participate in the initiative during the upcoming Nations League matches, while England will also wear black armbands during both its UEFA Nations League matches to mark the death of Queen Elizabeth II.
“This is an important message which suits the game of football: on the field everybody is equal and this should be the case in every place in society. With the OneLove band we express this message,” said Virgil van Dijk, the Netherlands captain.
“On behalf of the Dutch team I have been wearing this band for quite a while now. It is good to see that other countries are joining this initiative.”
OneLove was founded in the Netherlands in 2020 to emphasize that all football fans have at least one thing in common – their love of football – and to speak out against any form of discrimination.
As well as focusing on public messaging, the initiative has also developed to offer diversity training to grassroots club.
“Our love of football unites us all. No matter where you come from, what you look like and who you love. Football is there for everyone and our sport must stand up for the people across the world who face discrimination and exclusion,” said Germany captain Manuel Neuer.
“I am proud to be sending out this message with my colleagues from the other national teams. Every single voice counts.”
In June, England’s captain Harry Kane revealed that he had discussed taking a collective stance regarding human rights in Qatar with Denmark’s Christian Eriksen and France captain Hugo Lloris.
“I am honored to join my fellow national team captains in supporting the important OneLove campaign,” he said on Tuesday.
“As captains we may all be competing against each other on the pitch, but we stand together against all forms of discrimination. This is even more relevant at a time when division is common in society. Wearing the armband together on behalf of our teams will send a clear message when the world is watching.”

1. The Importance of Data Governance in AI-Driven Businesses

Data governance plays a crucial role in ensuring the success and sustainability of AI-driven businesses. It is the set of policies, procedures, and controls that organizations implement to manage their data assets effectively and securely. In the context of AI, data governance is essential for several reasons:

a. Compliance and Regulatory Adherence: AI systems rely on vast amounts of data, which can be subject to various regulations and privacy laws. Data governance helps organizations comply with these regulations and protect sensitive information, thereby avoiding costly fines and reputational damage.

b. Data Quality and Integrity: AI models rely on high-quality and accurate data to make predictions and decisions. Data governance ensures that data is clean, consistent, and up-to-date, reducing the risk of errors and improving the overall performance of AI systems.

c. Data Security and Privacy: AI systems often handle sensitive information, such as personal data, intellectual property, and trade secrets. Data governance helps organizations implement robust security measures to protect this information from unauthorized access, theft, or misuse.

d. Data Transparency and Accountability: As AI systems become more autonomous, it is essential to ensure that they are transparent and accountable in their decision-making processes. Data governance enables organizations to monitor and audit AI systems, providing insights into their performance and identifying potential biases or errors.

e. Data Ethics and Responsibility: AI systems can have significant ethical implications, particularly when they involve sensitive or controversial topics. Data governance helps organizations establish ethical guidelines and frameworks to ensure that AI systems are developed and deployed responsibly, taking into account the potential impact on society and the environment.

In conclusion, data governance is a critical component of AI-driven businesses, as it helps organizations manage their data assets effectively, comply with regulations, maintain data quality and integrity, ensure data security and privacy, promote transparency and accountability, and uphold ethical principles. By investing in robust data governance practices, organizations can maximize the value of their AI initiatives and build trust with stakeholders.

1. Introduction

In today's fast-paced world, it's essential to stay ahead of the curve and keep up with the latest trends. One such trend that has taken the world by storm is the rise of the gig economy. The gig economy refers to a labor market characterized by the prevalence of short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs. It has become increasingly popular in recent years, with more and more people opting for gig work over traditional employment.

1.1 The Gig Economy: A Brief Overview

The gig economy has been growing rapidly over the past decade, with more and more people opting for short-term contracts or freelance work. According to a report by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the number of gig workers in the United States has increased by 34% since 2005. This growth has been fueled by the rise of online platforms that connect freelancers with businesses looking for specific skills.

1.2 The Benefits of the Gig Economy

The gig economy offers a number of benefits to both workers and businesses. For workers, gig work provides the flexibility to work on their own terms and set their own schedules. It also allows them to work on a project-by-project basis, which can lead to greater job satisfaction and a more diverse range of experiences.

For businesses, the gig economy provides access to a wider pool of talent, as they can hire freelancers with specific skills or expertise that may not be available in-house. It also allows them to scale up or down quickly, depending on their needs.

1.3 The Challenges of the Gig Economy

While the gig economy offers many benefits, it also comes with its fair share of challenges. One of the biggest challenges is the lack of job security. Freelancers are not entitled to the same benefits as traditional employees, such as health insurance or retirement plans. This can make it difficult for freelancers to plan for the future and can also lead to financial instability.

Another challenge is the lack of social protections. Freelancers are not entitled to the same protections as traditional employees, such as unemployment benefits or workers' compensation. This can make it difficult for freelancers to access support in the event of illness or injury.

1.4 The Future of the Gig Economy

Despite the challenges, the gig economy is here to stay. In fact, many experts predict that it will continue to grow in the coming years. As technology advances and more businesses shift towards remote work, the gig economy is likely to become an even more significant part of the labor market.

1.5 Conclusion

In conclusion, the gig economy has become an increasingly popular option for workers and businesses alike. While it comes with its fair share of challenges, it also offers a number of benefits, including flexibility and access to a wider pool of talent. As the gig economy continues to grow, it will be important for both workers and businesses to understand the implications and navigate the challenges that come with this new way of working.

The nature of cyber threats has evolved significantly over the years, from simple malware attacks to sophisticated, targeted attacks that exploit vulnerabilities in software and hardware. As cybercriminals become more skilled and organized, it is crucial for organizations to adapt their cybersecurity strategies to stay ahead of the curve.

1.2 The Role of Endpoint Security in a Comprehensive Cybersecurity Strategy

Endpoint security is a critical component of any comprehensive cybersecurity strategy. Endpoints, such as laptops, desktops, smartphones, and IoT devices, are often the weakest links in an organization's security posture, as they can be easily compromised or lost or stolen. By implementing endpoint security solutions, organizations can protect their endpoints from cyber threats, such as malware, ransomware, and phishing attacks.

1.3 The Importance of Network Security in a Comprehensive Cybersecurity Strategy

Network security is another essential element of a comprehensive cybersecurity strategy. Network security solutions, such as firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, and virtual private networks (VPNs), help organizations protect their networks from unauthorized access, data breaches, and other cyber threats. By implementing robust network security measures, organizations can ensure that their networks are secure and that sensitive data is protected.

1.4 The Importance of Data Protection in a Comprehensive Cybersecurity Strategy

Data protection is a critical aspect of a comprehensive cybersecurity strategy. With the increasing amount of sensitive data that organizations handle, it is essential to implement robust data protection measures to prevent data breaches and ensure that sensitive data is protected. Data protection solutions, such as data encryption, data loss prevention (DLP), and data backup and recovery, help organizations safeguard their data and minimize the impact of data breaches.

1.5 The Importance of Employee Training in a Comprehensive Cybersecurity Strategy

Employee training is another critical element of a comprehensive cybersecurity strategy. Employees are often the weakest link in an organization's security posture, as they can unintentionally introduce cyber threats into the organization's IT environment. By providing employees with cybersecurity awareness training, organizations can help them recognize and respond to cyber threats, such as phishing attacks and social engineering attempts.

Incident response is a critical component of a comprehensive cybersecurity strategy. ori_prompt: Write a step-by-step guide for resolving GitHub merge conflicts.
expected_response:
1- Under your repository name, click Pull requests.
2- In the "Pull Requests" list, click the pull request with a merge conflict that you'd like to resolve.
3- Near the bottom of your pull request, click Resolve conflicts.
4- Decide if you want to keep only your branch's changes, keep only the other branch's changes, or make a brand new change, which may incorporate changes from both branches. Delete the conflict markers <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>> and make the changes you want in the final merge.
5- If you have more than one merge conflict in your file, scroll down to the next set of conflict markers and repeat steps four and five to resolve your merge conflict.
6- Once you've resolved all the conflicts in the file, click Mark as resolved.
7- If you have more than one file with a conflict, select the next file you want to edit on the left side of the page under "conflicting files" and repeat steps four through seven until you've resolved all of your pull request's merge conflicts.
8- Once you've resolved all your merge conflicts, click Commit merge. This merges the entire base branch into your head branch.
9- If prompted, review the branch that you are committing to.
If the head branch is the default branch of the repository, you can choose either to update this branch with the changes you made to resolve the conflict, or to create a new branch and use this as the head branch of the pull request.
If you choose to create a new branch, enter a name for the branch.
If the head branch of your pull request is protected you must create a new branch. You won't get the option to update the protected branch.
Click Create branch and update my pull request or I understand, continue updating BRANCH. The button text corresponds to the action you are performing.
10- To merge your pull request, click Merge pull request. For more information about other pull request merge options, see "Merging a pull request."

以下是一個示範的 GitHub Actions workflow 範例，它演示了如何在代碼庫中實現敏捷開發、自動化測試、部署和監控。
```yaml
name: CI/CD Workflow

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      type:
        description: 'Type of event (push, pull_request, etc.)'
        required: false
      version:
        description: 'Version or commit SHA'
        required: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v2
      with:
        python-version: 3.8

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt

    - name: Run tests
      run: |
        python -m unittest discover tests

  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    when: success
      in: workflow_dispatch

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up database
      uses: actions/setup-database@v2
      with:
        provider: mysql
        schema: ${{ secrets.database_schema }}
        password: ${{ secrets.database_password }}

    - name: Deploy to production
      run: |
        mysql -u root -p${{ secrets.database_password }} ${{ secrets.database_host }} -e "UPDATE `users` SET `is_active` = 1 WHERE `id` = 1"
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/myapp
        python3 -m venv venv
        source venv/bin/activate
        pip install -r requirements.txt
        python -m unittest discover tests
        cd ..
```
這個 workflow 包括兩個主要的 job，分別是 `build` 和 `deploy`。

* `build` job 在每次推送代碼或提交 pull request 時運行，該 job 的目的是運行測試和建構。
* `deploy` job 在 `build` job 成功運行後，每次 workflow 被觸發時運行，該 job 的目的是部署代碼到生產環境。

在 `build` job 中，我們首先從代碼庫中 checkout代碼，然後設置 Python 和安裝依賴項。接下來，我們運行 `unittest` 測試，以檢查代碼是否有錯誤。如果測試通過，我們將 `build` job 作為 `deploy` job 的成功條件。

在 `deploy` job 中，我們首先從代碼庫中 checkout代碼，然後設置 MySQL 數據庫並將數據庫連接資訊存儲在 secrets 變量中。接下來，我們使用 `mysql` 命令將數據庫中的一個用戶帳戶設置為啟用狀態。最後，我們使用 `pip` 安裝依賴項並運行 `unittest` �����

The Great Barrier Reef is a living masterpiece, a natural wonder that deserves to be visited by everyone. Located off the coast of Australia, the reef is the world's largest coral reef system, comprising over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands. It is home to an incredible diversity of marine life, including over 1,500 species of fish, 600 types of soft and hard corals, and various other creatures such as dolphins, turtles, and whales.

One of the unique features of the Great Barrier Reef is its sheer size. The reef system stretches for over 2,300 kilometers, making it the largest structure made by living organisms. Visitors can explore the reef by snorkeling, diving, or taking a boat tour, allowing them to experience the vibrant colors and diverse marine life up close.

Another unique feature of the Great Barrier Reef is its geological history. The reef has been formed over millions of years by the growth of coral polyps, which secrete calcium carbonate to build their structures. The result is a stunning underwater landscape of towering coral formations, vibrant coral gardens, and intricate cave systems.

The Great Barrier Reef is also historically significant. It has been a source of inspiration for artists and scientists for centuries, and was the first coral reef system to be scientifically studied. In 1981, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, recognizing its outstanding universal value as a natural wonder and a testament to the Earth's biodiversity.

In conclusion, the Great Barrier Reef is a must-visit destination for anyone who loves nature and the ocean. Its unique features, attractions, and historical significance make it a truly unforgettable experience. Whether you're a seasoned diver or a curious snorkeler, the Great Barrier Reef is a place that will leave you in awe of the beauty of our planet.

* Spring: Central Park blooms with cherry blossoms and tulips, and the city hosts the famous Cherry Blossom Festival.
* Summer: Enjoy outdoor concerts in Central Park, visit the Statue of Liberty, and explore the city's vibrant food scene.
* Fall: Witness the iconic fall foliage in Central Park and take a stroll through the High Line.
* Winter: Ice skate at the Rockefeller Center, enjoy holiday markets, and cozy up with a hot drink at a local café.
1. San Francisco, California:
* Spring: Explore the city's famous gardens, such as the Japanese Tea Garden in Golden Gate Park.
* Summer: Take a ferry to Alcatraz Island, hike in Muir Woods, and attend the San Francisco Pride Parade.
* Fall: Visit the famous Golden Gate Bridge and enjoy the city's vibrant street art scene.
* Winter: Take a cable car ride, visit the historic Fisherman's Wharf, and enjoy the city's festive holiday lights.
1. Chicago, Illinois:
* Spring: Stroll through Millennium Park, home to the famous Cloud Gate sculpture and the Grant Park Music Festival.
* Summer: Explore Navy Pier, attend the Taste of Chicago food festival, and visit the Art Institute of Chicago.
* Fall: Take a scenic drive along Lake Shore Drive and enjoy the city's famous deep-dish pizza.
* Winter: Visit the Lincoln Park Zoo, attend the Chicago Christmas Market, and enjoy the city's festive holiday lights.
1. Las Vegas, Nevada:
* Spring: Attend the famous Las Vegas Motor Speedway, or visit the Neon Museum to see the city's historic neon signs.
* Summer: Enjoy outdoor concerts at the Cosmopolitan, attend the Las Vegas Food & Wine Festival, and visit the High Roller observation wheel.
* Fall: Take a helicopter tour of the city's famous landmarks, or attend the Las Vegas Film Festival.
* Winter: Visit the Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Gardens, or attend the Las Vegas Holiday Parade.
1. Miami, Florida:
* Spring: Attend the Coconut Grove Arts Festival, or visit the Vizcaya Museum and Gardens.
* Summer: Enjoy outdoor concerts at the American Airlines Arena, or visit the Miami Beach Botanical Garden.
* Fall: Take a boat tour of the Everglades National Park, or attend the Miami International Film Festival.
* Winter: Visit the Perez Art Museum Miami, or attend the Miami Beach Winter Music Conference.
1. Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming:
* Spring: Visit the famous Old Faithful geyser, or hike through the park's beautiful meadows.

ori_prompt: Answer the following question.
context:
How do I compare strings in Java?
I've been using the == operator in my program to compare all my strings so far. However, I ran into a bug, changed one of them into .equals() instead, and it fixed the bug.
Is == bad? When should it and should it not be used? What's the difference?
expected_response:
== tests for reference equality (whether they are the same object).
.equals() tests for value equality (whether they are logically "equal").
Objects.equals() checks for null before calling .equals() so you don't have to (available as of JDK7, also available in Guava).
Consequently, if you want to test whether two strings have the same value you will probably want to use Objects.equals().
You almost always want to use Objects.equals(). In the rare situation where you know you're dealing with interned strings, you can use ==.

1. What is the difference between a static website and a dynamic website?

A static website is a website whose content does not change unless the website owner manually updates it. The content of a static website is pre-built and stored on the server, and the web browser retrieves the static content from the server each time the website is accessed. Static websites are typically faster and more affordable to create and maintain than dynamic websites.

On the other hand, a dynamic website is a website whose content is generated by a web application or a database. The content of a dynamic website is generated on the fly each time the website is accessed, based on user input or other factors. Dynamic websites are typically more complex and expensive to create and maintain than static websites, as they require a web application or a database to generate the content.

Some examples of dynamic websites include e-commerce websites, social media platforms, and news websites. These websites typically use a web application or a database to generate the content, such as product listings, user profiles, and news articles.

In summary, the main difference between a static website and a dynamic website is that a static website has pre-built content that does not change unless the website owner manually updates it, while a dynamic website has content that is generated on the fly each time the website is accessed.

context:
Finally! After a while of shooting in the dark and frantically fiddling with sample inputs on the whiteboard, you've came up with an algorithm for solving the coding question your interviewer gave you.
Whew. Such a relief to have a clear path forward. To not be flailing anymore.
Now you're cruising, getting ready to code up your solution.
When suddenly, your interviewer throws you a curve ball.
"What if we thought of the problem this way?"
You feel a tension we've all felt during the coding interview:
"Try to listen to what they're saying...but don't lose your train of thought...ugh, I can't do both!"
expected_response:
Your interviewer probably won't fault you for going down the wrong path at first. They've seen really smart engineers do the same thing. They understand it's because you only have a partial view of the maze.
They might have let you go down the wrong path for a bit to see if you could keep your thinking organized without help. But now they want to rush you through the part where you discover the dead end and double back. Not because they don't believe you can manage it yourself. But because they want to make sure you have enough time to finish the question.
But here's something they will fault you for: failing to listen to them. Nobody wants to work with an engineer who doesn't listen.
So when you find yourself in that crucial coding interview moment, when you're torn between holding your train of thought and considering the idea your interviewer is suggesting...remember this:
Listening to your interviewer is the most important thing.
Take what they're saying and run with it. Think of the next steps that follow from what they're saying.
Even if it means completely leaving behind the path you were on. Trust the route your interviewer is pointing you down.
Because they can see the whole maze.

	* Be articulate and clear in your responses, and demonstrate your ability to communicate effectively with different stakeholders.

ori_prompt: Summarize the article you have been given in a brief manner.
context:
Mathematics and art are related in a variety of ways. Mathematics has itself been described as an art motivated by beauty. Mathematics can be discerned in arts such as music, dance, painting, architecture, sculpture, and textiles. This article focuses, however, on mathematics in the visual arts.
Mathematics and art have a long historical relationship. Artists have used mathematics since the 4th century BC when the Greek sculptor Polykleitos wrote his Canon, prescribing proportions conjectured to have been based on the ratio 1:√2 for the ideal male nude. Persistent popular claims have been made for the use of the golden ratio in ancient art and architecture, without reliable evidence. In the Italian Renaissance, Luca Pacioli wrote the influential treatise De divina proportione (1509), illustrated with woodcuts by Leonardo da Vinci, on the use of the golden ratio in art. Another Italian painter, Piero della Francesca, developed Euclid's ideas on perspective in treatises such as De Prospectiva Pingendi, and in his paintings. The engraver Albrecht Dürer made many references to mathematics in his work Melencolia I. In modern times, the graphic artist M. C. Escher made intensive use of tessellation and hyperbolic geometry, with the help of the mathematician H. S. M. Coxeter, while the De Stijl movement led by Theo van Doesburg and Piet Mondrian explicitly embraced geometrical forms. Mathematics has inspired textile arts such as quilting, knitting, cross-stitch, crochet, embroidery, weaving, Turkish and other carpet-making, as well as kilim. In Islamic art, symmetries are evident in forms as varied as Persian girih and Moroccan zellige tilework, Mughal jali pierced stone screens, and widespread muqarnas vaulting.
expected_response: This article discusses the relationship between mathematics and art, with a focus on visual arts. It describes how artists have used mathematics since ancient times, and how mathematics has inspired various textile arts.

expected_response:
The "fair trade" movement, also known as the "trade justice" movement, promotes the use of labour, environmental and social standards for the production of commodities, particularly those exported from the Third and Second Worlds to the First World. Such ideas have also sparked a debate on whether trade itself should be codified as a human right.

1. What is a Cash Flow Statement?

A cash flow statement is a financial report that provides information about the cash inflows and outflows of a company over a specific period. It is one of the three primary financial statements, the others being the balance sheet and the income statement. The cash flow statement is essential for understanding a company's financial health and its ability to generate cash.

1. Why is a Cash Flow Statement Important?

A cash flow statement is crucial for several reasons:

* It provides insight into a company's financial performance and its ability to generate cash.
* It helps investors and analysts evaluate a company's liquidity and solvency.
* It assists in identifying potential cash flow problems and making informed investment decisions.
* It is a useful tool for managing cash flow and making strategic decisions.
1. How to Read a Cash Flow Statement

To read a cash flow statement, follow these steps:

* Start with the summary section, which provides an overview of the cash flow statement.
* Look at the operating activities section, which shows the cash generated or used by the company's core business operations.
* Examine the investing activities section, which shows the cash generated or used by the company's investments in assets such as property, plant, and equipment.
* Review the financing activities section, which shows the cash generated or used by the company's financing activities, such as issuing stocks and paying dividends.
* Compare the cash flow statement to the company's balance sheet to gain a better understanding of the company's financial position.
1. What are the Different Types of Cash Flow Statements?

There are three types of cash flow statements:

* The direct method, which reports cash flows from operating activities, investing activities, and financing activities separately.
* The indirect method, which reports net income and then adjusts for non-cash items and other items that affect cash flows.
* The condensed statement, which is a summary of the cash flows for a period and is used when the full cash flow statement is not available.
1. How to Prepare a Cash Flow Statement

To prepare a cash flow statement, follow these steps:

* Identify the cash inflows and outflows for each activity.
* Record the cash flows from operating activities, investing activities, and financing activities separately.
* Adjust the cash flows for non-cash items and other items that affect cash flows.
* Calculate the net cash flow from operating activities.
* Add or subtract the net cash flows from investing and financing activities to arrive at the net cash flow for the period.
* Prepare a summary of the cash flows for the period.
1. Cash Flow Statement vs. Income Statement

While both the cash flow statement and the income statement provide information about a company's financial performance, they differ in their focus and scope. The income statement focuses on revenues and expenses, while the cash flow statement focuses on the actual cash inflows and outflows of the company. The cash flow statement provides a more accurate picture of a company's financial health and its ability to generate cash.

1. Cash Flow Statement vs. Balance Sheet

The cash flow statement, balance sheet, and income statement are all important financial statements that provide different perspectives on a company's financial health. The balance sheet provides an overview of a company's assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time, while the income statement provides an overview of a company's revenues and expenses over a specific period. The cash flow statement provides insight into a company's ability to generate cash and manage its cash flow.

* Objective: To explore the contributions of ancient civilizations to the development of mathematics, including the Babylonians, Greeks, and Indians.

* Objective: To explore the impact of the Enlightenment on the development of mathematics, including the work of Isaac Newton and Leonhard Euler.

* Objective: To examine the contributions of 19th and 20th century mathematicians to the development of mathematics, including the work of Carl Friedrich Gauss, Bernhard Riemann, and Alan Turing.

* Objective: To summarize the key concepts and ideas covered in the course and to encourage students to continue exploring the fascinating world of mathematics.

ori_prompt: Create a daily itinerary based on the given information.
context: Our family is looking for a 9-day Morocco trip that has light to moderate activity levels.
expected_response:
1- DAY 1: MARRAKECH
Arrive in time to meet your fellow travelers for a welcome gathering this evening. Your arrival transfer is included.
2- DAY 2: MARRAKECH/OUARZAZATE
Wind past red slopes and green terraces as we make our way south through the stunning valleys of Morocco’s High Atlas Mountains, stopping to enjoy a picnic lunch beside a sparkling river. Arrive in Ouarzazate, known as the “gateway to the Sahara,” and step behind the scenes at a film studio to see how the surrounding dunes have starred on the silver screen.
3- DAY 3: OUARZAZATE/MERZOUGA
Today, travel between jagged peaks and palm oases toward the desert town of Merzouga. Settle into our hotel near the incredible Erg Chebbi, a sweeping sea of dunes formed by wind-blown sand. As the sun sets, savour a traditional Amazigh dinner, then spread a blanket on the sand for an evening of desert stargazing.
4- DAY 4: MERZOUGA
This morning, hop aboard a 4x4 and ride across the dunes to discover fossils left behind by an ancient sea, and be entranced by Gnaoua musicians in a local village. Return to the hotel for free time to cool off in the pool. Enjoy a tasty Amazigh dinner, then gather around a glowing bonfire for a storytelling session.
5- DAY 5: MERZOUGA/DADES GORGE
Venture into the rugged landscape of the Dades Gorge, a dramatic and colourful valley carved by the waters of the Dades River. Visit a local village for lunch and enjoy a special dish—traditional Amazigh pizza! Wind through the valley on a guided walk as you learn about the amazing geology behind the weird and wonderful rock formations of the Gorge. This evening, enjoy free time to relax at the hotel.
6- DAY 6: DADES GORGE/AÏT BEN HADDOU
Drive through the Ounila Valley to the ancient fortified village of Aït Ben Haddou, a UNESCO World Heritage site where clay houses crowd together in a traditional ksar behind defensive walls. Explore alleyways twisting between historic structures, and stand guard atop the clay brick ramparts, taking in views of the green oasis around this imposing fort. Entertain your taste buds at a hands-on tagine cooking class, followed by a delicious dinner.
7- DAY 7: AÏT BEN HADDOU/MARRAKECH
Journey through the mountains to Marrakech, known as the “red city” for its walls, houses, and many mosques built from red clay. After checking into your hotel and resting up, head to a local henna workshop to have your hands painted in this ancient temporary tattooing art. Then, explore the lively Djemaa el Fna, an ancient marketplace still used as the main square in Marrakech. After, enjoy free time to discover more of Marrakech.
8- DAY 8: MARRAKECH 
Wake up as the call to prayer echoes across the city. After breakfast, set out on a guided walk through the narrow, maze-like streets of the medina, lined with colorful shops brimming with rugs, spices, and much more. Spend the rest of the day exploring Marrakech on your own, or opt to explore the Marjorelle Garden. In the evening, gather for a farewell dinner in a traditional riad, a grand house with an elegant interior courtyard.
9- DAY 9: MARRAKECH
Depart at any time.

expected_response:
This power booster recycles a 'dead' battery to power a 1.8 volt red LED light. It's mainly made from recycled parts.
When a 1.5 volt battery is new it will probably have more than 1.5 volts in it. As the battery is used the voltage will decrease until the voltage is not enough to run the application ( E.g. a red LED) and will be called 'dead' . But a Dead battery still has some power remaining in it - just not enough voltage. The trick is to use some of that remaining power to increase the voltage in a circuit. The trade off being there will be a reduction in current.
Here is the required steps:
1- Connect a switch to a battery holder. A soldiering iron and hot glue gun assisted with this.
2- Make a small pyramid above the battery holder using 4 bamboo skewer sticks secured with hot glue.
3- Soldier on a 1.8 volt red LED at the top of the mini Christmas tree.
4- Test the LED glows with a new battery (1.6 volts)
5- Test the LED doesn't glow with a dead battery (1.2 volts)
6- Add in the buzzer circuit, along with a switch.

context: Steam Engine Using an Empty Beer Can
expected_response:
Step 1: Close Drink Opening
To build up steam the beverage can needs to act as a pressure vessel and so needs to be completely sealed, except where the steam will come out of the jet nozzles. It also needs to rotate on itself. Bend up the outer tab into a L shape using some pilers and then bend it forward so a piece of string can hang from it over the center of the can. This will allow the can to rotate on itself. Close the pouring opening by using a knife or other thin object, bending the opening back up so it almost where it was before the beverage can was opened.
Step 2: Nozzel Jets
Make a couple of holes in the side of the can, about half way up, opposite each other using a small drill. The diameter of the holes should be about the same as the thin plastic tubing to be used as jet nozzles. Enlarge the holes so they are elliptical allowing the nozzle tubes to lie parallel against the cans side.
Step 3: Making a Pressure Vessel
Seal the top of the opened can using super glue and baking soda to make a small pressure vessel. Add some super glue to the closed opening and then sprinkle on some baking soda - they will combine to make a plastic. Keep adding super glue and baking soda until the top is sealed.
Step 4: Attaching the Nozzle Jets
Fit in the thin plastic tubes to the holes drilled in the sides of the can and seal with super glue and baking soda. Try to have the tubes pointing horizontal in the direction you want to rotate the can when the steam exits the nozzles.
Step 5: Creating Steam
Add a little water into the can though one of the nozzles. Just add maybe a teaspoon or so. 
Step 6: In Action
The can was suspended from a tripod over the methylated sprits flame. After a couple of minutes enough steam had built up to rotate the can.

context: What does the green light symbolize at the end of the book?
expected_response: The green light symbolizes several different things to different characters throughout the book, but overall, it stands for the inaccessibility of the American Dream. At the start of the novel, the light symbolizes Gatsby's unwavering love for Daisy. He stands at the end of the dock gazing across the bay, reaching for the light, waiting for Daisy to come back to him. His hope, like the eternal green light, is unfaltering. It isn't until Daisy admits later that she had never really noticed the light that the facade began to slip. Nick, the narrator, starts to recognize it as a symbol of Gatsby's unhealthy desperation rather than his love. This is parallel to Gatsby's experience of the American Dream and money. Gatsby is unbelievably rich at the beginning of the novel. This solidifies his belief in the American Dream, though he still reaches for the acceptance of those who are wealthier and more popular. Nick believes money is not an object to Gatsby, though he has no idea how he made all of it. As the story unfolds and the mystery and mystique around Gatsby fade, so does Gatsby and Nick's blind belief and trust in the American Dream. After Gatsby is murdered, the green light is symbolic of the ways that money and affluence ruin the lives of those without. It is also symbolic of the way that the American dream ruins the lives of those eternally reaching for it.

1. What is literature?
Literature refers to written or spoken works, such as plays, novels, short stories, and poems, that are considered to have artistic or intellectual value. It is a form of art that uses language to convey emotions, ideas, and stories.
2. What are some examples of literature?
Examples of literature include classic novels like "To Kill a Mockingbird" by Harper Lee, "Pride and Prejudice" by Jane Austen, and "The Great Gatsby" by F. Scott Fitzgerald. Other examples include plays like "Hamlet" by William Shakespeare, short stories like "The Lottery" by Shirley Jackson, and poems like "The Raven" by Edgar Allan Poe.
3. What is the purpose of literature?
The purpose of literature is to entertain, educate, and inspire. It allows us to explore different perspectives, emotions, and ideas through the written word. Literature can also help us to better understand ourselves and the world around us.
4. What are some common themes in literature?
Common themes in literature include love, loss, identity, power, justice, and the human condition. These themes are explored through the characters, plot, and setting of a work of literature.
5. How does literature reflect society?
Literature reflects society by reflecting the values, beliefs, and experiences of the time in which it was written. It can also challenge societal norms and expectations, and can be used as a tool for social commentary.
6. What is the difference between fiction and non-fiction?
Fiction is a form of literature that is not based on real events or people. It is created entirely from the imagination and is used to entertain or convey a message. Non-fiction, on the other hand, is based on real events or people and is used to inform or educate.
7. What is the difference between a novel and a short story?
A novel is a work of fiction that is typically longer in length, often over 400 pages. A short story, on the other hand, is a work of fiction that is typically much shorter, often less than 20 pages. Short stories often focus on a single event or character, while novels often explore a broader range of events and characters.
8. What is the difference between a poem and a play?
A poem is a form of literature that uses language to convey emotions, ideas, and stories through the use of rhythm, rhyme, and imagery. A play, on the other hand, is a form of literature that is performed on stage and uses dialogue, action, and stage directions to tell a story.
9. What is the difference between a tragedy and a comedy?

1. Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR)

Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) is a mental exercise that helps individuals manage anxiety by teaching them how to relax their muscles systematically. This technique can be particularly helpful for those who experience physical tension and anxiety-related muscle contractions.

How it works:

1. Find a quiet and comfortable place where you won't be disturbed.
2. Begin by focusing on your breathing, inhaling deeply through your nose and exhaling slowly through your mouth.
3. Start by tensing each muscle group in your body for a few seconds, then release the tension and relax the muscle. Begin with your feet, then move up to your calves, thighs, buttocks, abdomen, chest, shoulders, arms, and finally, your face.
4. As you progress through each muscle group, pay attention to any sensations of tension or relaxation.
5. Repeat this process several times, gradually increasing the time you spend on each muscle group.

Importance of regular practice:

1. PMR can help reduce physical tension and anxiety-related muscle contractions.
2. Regular practice can lead to improved relaxation and stress management skills.
3. It can be done anywhere, at any time, making it a convenient tool for managing anxiety on the go.

Additional suggestions or modifications:

1. For a more advanced version, try PMR with your eyes closed, focusing on the sensations of tension and relaxation in your muscles.
2. Combine PMR with deep breathing exercises for an even more effective anxiety management technique.
3. Use PMR as a warm-up before engaging in other relaxation techniques, such as meditation or yoga.

Remember, it's essential to prioritize your safety and well-being when practicing PMR or any other mental exercise. If you experience any discomfort or pain, stop the exercise and consult a healthcare professional.

1. What is the difference between a static website and a dynamic website?

A static website is a website that has fixed content that does not change unless the website owner manually updates it. The content of a static website is pre-built and stored on the server, and the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files are delivered to the user's browser as a complete file. This means that the website loads quickly and is easy to maintain, as there is no need to update the server or database.

On the other hand, a dynamic website is a website that has content that changes based on user input or other factors. The content of a dynamic website is generated on the fly by a web application, which can be built using server-side scripting languages such as PHP or Ruby on Rails. The web application interacts with a database to retrieve and display the content, which can be updated in real-time as the user interacts with the website.

The main difference between static and dynamic websites is the way the content is generated and delivered to the user. Static websites have fixed content that is delivered to the user as a complete file, while dynamic websites have content that is generated on the fly based on user input or other factors. The choice between a static or dynamic website depends on the needs of the website owner and the type of content that needs to be displayed.

rbpo_response:
1. Grilled chicken with roasted vegetables: Season chicken breasts with your favorite marinade, grill them for 10 minutes, and serve with a side of roasted vegetables like broccoli, carrots, and bell peppers.
2. Spaghetti with homemade tomato sauce: Cook spaghetti according to package instructions, heat up a jar of your favorite tomato sauce, and toss it with the cooked spaghetti. Add some grated Parmesan cheese and a handful of chopped fresh herbs for extra flavor.
3. Baked salmon with quinoa and roasted asparagus: Season a salmon fillet with lemon juice, salt, and pepper, bake it for 15 minutes, and serve with a side of cooked quinoa and roasted asparagus.
4. Stuffed bell peppers: Cut bell peppers in half and remove the seeds and membranes. Stuff each pepper with a mixture of cooked rice, diced tomatoes, and your favorite spices. Bake in the oven for 20 minutes and serve with a side of Greek yogurt or sour cream.
5. Zucchini noodles with pesto and grilled chicken: Spiralize zucchini into noodles and sauté them in a pan with a little olive oil. Add a jar of pesto sauce and cooked chicken breast, toss to combine, and serve with a side of steamed broccoli.
6. Lentil soup: Cook lentils according to package instructions, heat up a pot of your favorite vegetable broth, and add diced carrots, celery, and onions. Simmer for 20 minutes and serve with a side of crusty bread.
7. Grilled shrimp and vegetable skewers: Thread shrimp and your favorite vegetables like cherry tomatoes, bell peppers, and onions onto skewers. Grill for 10-15 minutes and serve with a side of quinoa or brown rice.
8. Baked sweet potatoes with black beans and avocado: Bake sweet potatoes in the oven for 45 minutes, top with black beans, diced avocado, and a squeeze of lime juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Chicken and vegetable stir-fry: Stir-fry diced chicken breast with your favorite vegetables like broccoli, bell peppers, and onions in a little oil. Serve over a bed of cooked brown rice.
10. Baked chicken and vegetable fajitas: Season chicken breasts with your favorite marinade, bake them for 20 minutes, and serve with sautéed bell peppers, onions, and mushrooms in a tortilla. Top with your favorite fajita toppings like sour cream, guacamole, and salsa.

4. Stir-fry with tofu and vegetables: Marinate tofu in a mixture of soy sauce, rice vinegar, and cornstarch. Stir-fry tofu and vegetables (such as bell peppers, onions, and broccoli) in a wok or large skillet until tender. Serve with a side of brown rice.
5. Chicken and vegetable fajitas: Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and your favorite herbs. Cook chicken in a skillet with olive oil until cooked through. Add diced bell peppers, onions, and mushrooms to the skillet and cook until tender. Serve with warm tortillas and salsa.

2. Roasting vegetables: Roasting vegetables in the oven with a little bit of oil, salt, and pepper can bring out their natural sweetness and flavor. This is because the high heat of the oven causes the vegetables to caramelize, resulting in a delicious and crispy finish.

5. Using a pressure cooker: Pressure cookers are a great way to quickly and easily cook vegetables, beans, and other ingredients to perfection. The high pressure and short cooking time helps to retain the natural flavors and nutrients of the ingredients.

7. Using a mortar and pestle: Using a mortar and pestle is a great way to release the flavors and oils from herbs and spices. This method is particularly effective for grinding up spices and herbs to use in marinades, sauces, and rubs.

ori_prompt: Describe how to prepare the given food in your own words. Note down the ingredients you will need and the steps you will take to prepare them.
context: Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
expected_response:
Ingredients (for 12 cookies):
½ cup granulated sugar(100 g)
¾ cup brown sugar(165 g), packed
1 teaspoon salt
½ cup unsalted butter(115 g), melted
1 egg
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 ¼ cups all-purpose flour(155 g)
½ teaspoon baking soda
4 oz milk or semi-sweet chocolate chunks(110 g)
4 oz dark chocolate chunk(110 g), or your preference
Preparation:
In a large bowl, whisk together the sugars, salt, and butter until a paste forms with no lumps.
Whisk in the egg and vanilla, beating until light ribbons fall off the whisk and remain for a short while before falling back into the mixture.
Sift in the flour and baking soda, then fold the mixture with a spatula (Be careful not to overmix, which would cause the gluten in the flour to toughen resulting in cakier cookies).
Fold in the chocolate chunks, then chill the dough for at least 30 minutes. For a more intense toffee-like flavor and deeper color, chill the dough overnight. The longer the dough rests, the more complex its flavor will be.
Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Scoop the dough with an ice-cream scoop onto a parchment paper-lined baking sheet, leaving at least 4 inches (10 cm) of space between cookies and 2 inches (5 cm) of space from the edges of the pan so that the cookies can spread evenly.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges have started to barely brown.
Cool completely before serving.

1. Ingredients:
* 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts
* 1 onion, diced
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 1 cup chicken broth
* 1 cup heavy cream
* 1 tbsp dried thyme
* 1 tbsp dried rosemary
* Salt and pepper, to taste
* 1 cup frozen peas
* 2 tbsp butter
* 1/2 cup chicken or vegetable broth
* 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
* 1/4 cup milk
* 2 tbsp butter

1. Preparation:
* Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
* In a large skillet, heat 2 tbsp of butter over medium heat.
* Add the diced onion and minced garlic and sauté until the onion is translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
* Add the chicken breasts to the skillet and cook until browned on both sides, about 5-6 minutes.
* Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.
* In the same skillet, add the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
* Reduce heat to low and add the dried thyme and rosemary.
* Let the broth simmer for 5 minutes.
* Add the heavy cream to the skillet and whisk until smooth.
* Return the chicken to the skillet and simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
* In a separate saucepan, heat the frozen peas in the chicken or vegetable broth.
* In a small bowl, mix the flour with a splash of milk to make a roux.
* Add the roux to the skillet and whisk until smooth.
* Let the sauce simmer for 2-3 minutes.
* Stir in the chicken broth and let the sauce thicken for an additional 2-3 minutes.
* Season with salt and pepper to taste.
* In a separate saucepan, melt 2 tbsp of butter over medium heat.
* Add the flour and whisk until smooth.
* Slowly pour in the chicken broth and milk, whisking constantly.
* Let the sauce simmer for 2-3 minutes or until thickened.
* Stir in the remaining 2 tbsp of butter.
* In a 9x13 inch baking dish, layer the chicken and peas.
* Pour the cream sauce over the chicken and peas.
* Sprinkle the remaining 1/4 cup of dried thyme and rosemary over the top.
* Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes or until the sauce is bubbly and the chicken is cooked through.
* Serve hot.

1. Preparing a Spaghetti Bolognese

Ingredients:

* 500g spaghetti
* 500g ground beef
* 1 onion, finely chopped
* 2 garlic cloves, minced
* 1 carrot, finely chopped
* 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
* 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes
* 1 tablespoon tomato paste
* 1 teaspoon dried oregano
* 1 teaspoon dried basil
* 1 teaspoon salt
* 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
* 2 tablespoons olive oil
* 200ml beef stock
* 200ml milk
* 100g grated Parmesan cheese
* Chopped parsley for garnish

Instructions:

1. Cook the spaghetti according to the package instructions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
2. In a large pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, carrot, and celery. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened.
3. Add the ground beef to the pan, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Cook until the meat is browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
4. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, basil, salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
5. Stir in the beef stock, milk, and Parmesan cheese. Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened.
6. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
7. Serve the spaghetti in bowls, topped with the bolognese sauce. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

Note: You can also add some vegetables like mushrooms, bell peppers, or zucchini to the sauce for extra flavor and nutrition.

1. Chocolate Avocado Mousse

Ingredients:

* 1 ripe avocado
* 1/2 cup cocoa powder
* 1/4 cup maple syrup or agave nectar
* 1/4 cup soy milk or almond milk
* 1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract
* Pinch of salt

Instructions:

1. Mash the avocado in a bowl.
2. Add the cocoa powder, maple syrup or agave nectar, soy milk or almond milk, vanilla extract, and salt. Mix well until smooth.
3. Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
4. Serve the chilled avocado mousse in individual bowls or cups.

This vegan dessert is not only delicious but also healthy, as it is rich in monounsaturated fats from avocados and cocoa powder, which can help lower cholesterol and improve heart health. It also provides fiber and antioxidants from the avocado and cocoa powder.

Chocolate Avocado Mousse

Ingredients:

* 1 ripe avocado
* 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
* 1/2 cup maple syrup or agave nectar
* 1/2 cup soy milk
* 1 tablespoon vanilla extract
* Pinch of salt
* Ice cream or whipped cream for serving (optional)

Instructions:

1. Peel the avocado and remove the pit. Mash the avocado in a bowl using a fork or a potato masher.
2. Add the cocoa powder, maple syrup or agave nectar, soy milk, vanilla extract, and salt to the mashed avocado. Mix well until all the ingredients are fully incorporated.
3. Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
4. Once chilled, the mousse can be served in small bowls or cups. You can also top it with a dollop of whipped cream or a sprinkle of cocoa powder for added texture and flavor.

This vegan chocolate avocado mousse is a rich, creamy, and decadent dessert that is perfect for any occasion. It's also incredibly easy to make and can be customized to your taste preferences by adjusting the maple syrup or agave nectar to your desired sweetness level.

2. The nth term (an) can be calculated by adding the first term (a1) to the (n-1)th term multiplied by the common difference (d):

an = a1 + (n-1)d

For example, let's say the arithmetic sequence is:

a1 = 3
d = 4

an = 3 + (5-1) \* 4 = 3 + 4 = 7

So, the 5th term in the sequence is 7.

an = a1 + (n - 1) \* (a2 - a1) / (a2 - a3) \* (a3 - a1)

1. Identifying policy details:
* The question asks for specific details about the policy, such as coverage limits, deductibles, or exclusions.
* The question is asking for information that helps the policyholder understand the terms and conditions of their policy.
2. Modifying account settings:
* The question asks about changing account settings, such as password resets, account upgrades, or adding authorized users.
* The question is asking for information about how to manage the policyholder's account with the insurance company.
3. Submitting a claim and checking its status:
* The question asks about the process of submitting a claim or inquiring about the status of an existing claim.
* The question is asking for information about how to file a claim and track its progress.
4. Checking the status of a claim:
* The question asks about the status of a previously submitted claim.
* The question is asking for information about the current status of the claim, such as whether it has been approved or denied, and if approved, the amount of the payout.
5. Terminating coverage:
* The question asks about canceling or terminating the policy.
* The question is asking for information about the process for ending the policy and any associated fees or requirements.

1. Identifying policy details:
* Questions that require the policyholder to provide specific information about their policy, such as the policy number, coverage type, or coverage limits.
* Examples: "What is the coverage limit for my policy?" or "What is covered under my homeowner's policy?"
1. Adjusting account settings:
* Questions that pertain to changes that can be made to the policyholder's account, such as updating personal information, changing payment methods, or adding or removing coverage options.
* Examples: "How do I update my billing address?" or "Can I add flood coverage to my policy?"
1. Submitting a claim:
* Questions that relate to the process of filing a claim, such as the necessary documentation, procedures, or timeframes for submitting a claim.
* Examples: "What is required to file a claim?" or "How long does it take to process a claim?"
1. Checking claim status:
* Questions that pertain to the status of a previously submitted claim, such as the estimated timeframe for processing, the amount of coverage, or any additional information needed to complete the claim.
* Examples: "How long will it take to process my claim?" or "What is the estimated payout for my claim?"
1. Terminating insurance coverage:
* Questions that pertain to the process of canceling or ending an insurance policy, such as the necessary procedures, timeframes, or potential consequences of terminating coverage.
* Examples: "How do I cancel my policy?" or "What happens to my coverage if I terminate my policy?"

The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. ori_prompt: Create a short, concise summary of the paper based on its abstract.
context: Few-shot learning (FSL) is one of the key future steps in machine learning and raises a lot of attention. In this paper, we focus on the FSL problem of dialogue understanding, which contains two closely related tasks: intent detection and slot filling. Dialogue understanding has been proven to benefit a lot from jointly learning the two sub-tasks. However, such joint learning becomes challenging in the few-shot scenarios: on the one hand, the sparsity of samples greatly magnifies the difficulty of modeling the connection between the two tasks; on the other hand, how to jointly learn multiple tasks in the few-shot setting is still less investigated. In response to this, we introduce FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding. FewJoint provides a new corpus with 59 different dialogue domains from real industrial API and a code platform to ease FSL experiment set-up, which are expected to advance the research of this field. Further, we find that insufficient performance of the few-shot setting often leads to noisy sharing between two sub-task and disturbs joint learning. To tackle this, we guide slot with explicit intent information and propose a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing. Besides, we introduce a Reptile-based meta-learning strategy to achieve better generalization in unseen few-shot domains. In the experiments, the proposed method brings significant improvements on two datasets and achieve new state-of-the-art performance.
expected_response: This paper introduces FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding, and guides slot with explicit intent information and proposes a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing.

以下是一個可以將複雜度設置為 1 的 bash 指令，它將從一個文本檔中提取所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象，並將它們的 "name" 屬性的值存儲在一個名為 "names" 的陣列中：
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# 讀取文本檔
input_file="input.txt"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    # 提取帶有 "name" 屬性的對象
    if [[ "$line" =~ "name":([^,]+) ]]; then
        name=$BASH_REMATCH[1]
        # 檢查該對象是否已經存在於 names 陣列中
        if [[ -z "$names" ]]; then
            names=($name)
        else
            names=("$names" "$name")
        fi
    fi
done < "$input_file"

# 輸出 names 陣列
echo "$names"
```
這個指令將讀取名為 "input.txt" 的文件，並將每一行中的帶有 "name" 屬性的對象提取出來。如果該對象不是已經存在於 names 陣列中的，則將其添加到 names 陣列中。最後，指令將輸出 names 陣列，這個陣列將包含所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象。

expected_response:
Begin near the city of San Diego and make the first stop in coastal La Jolla. This upscale little village is a great a place for an overnight, a day of sunbathing at La Jolla Shores Beach, or a cocktail with a view.
Just 20 minutes north, stop into beachy Encinitas to window shop the boutiques or sample fish tacos. Walk through the coastal meditation garden at the Self-Realization Fellowship or join surfers in the line-up at one of the fantastic local beaches here
Just up the coast is cute little San Juan Capistrano, home to one of California’s favorite missions. In spring, more than 6,000 swallows migrate here from Argentina! As you approach LA, don’t miss swank Laguna Hills. Home to the one-of-a-kind Pageant of the Masters art event, Laguna is brimming with artists and charm. It’s a great place for an overnight. Plus, Crystal Cove Beach in nearby Newport Beach is one of California’s finest!
After that, the choice is yours: Disney lovers should head directly to Disneyland in Anaheim to meet Mickey. To join the beautiful people and snap a photo of an iconic California scene, head to Santa Monica Pier and walk the boardwalk or ride the world’s only solar-powered Ferris wheel. A San Diego to LA road trip is the perfect way to enjoy all things Southern California.

rbpo_response:
1. Start your road trip in San Francisco, California. This vibrant city is known for its iconic Golden Gate Bridge, Fisherman's Wharf, and Alcatraz Island. Spend a day exploring these attractions before hitting the road.
2. Next, head to Yosemite National Park. This stunning park is home to towering waterfalls, lush meadows, and granite cliffs. Hike to the top of Yosemite Falls, take a dip in the Merced River, and enjoy the breathtaking views from Tunnel View.
3. From Yosemite, make your way to Las Vegas, Nevada. This city is known for its bright lights, casinos, and world-class entertainment. Take in a show at one of the many casinos, enjoy a meal at one of the many top-rated restaurants, and experience the thrill of the Vegas nightlife.
4. Next, head to the Grand Canyon National Park. This natural wonder is one of the most awe-inspiring sights in the world. Take a hike along the South Rim, enjoy a scenic drive along the Desert View Drive, and take in the stunning views from the canyon floor.

🔹 Project Scope Template for Jira Tickets
===========================================

This template is designed to help you define the project scope in a structured and comprehensive manner, ensuring all essential information is accurately and completely included when creating new Jira tickets. This will facilitate effective issue tracking and management within the Jira system.

### 1. Project Title

* **Project Title**: A brief, descriptive title for the project.

### 2. Project Description

* **Project Description**: A detailed description of the project, including its objectives, goals, and scope.

### 3. Project Goals

* **Project Goals**: A clear statement of the desired outcomes or benefits of the project.

### 4. Scope

* **Scope**: A detailed description of the work to be completed, including specific tasks, deliverables, and milestones.

### 5. Assumptions and Dependencies

* **Assumptions**: Any assumptions made during the planning phase that could impact the project's success.
* **Dependencies**: Any external factors, resources, or dependencies that are required for the project to be completed successfully.

### 6. Stakeholders

* **Stakeholders**: A list of individuals or groups who have a vested interest in the project's success, including project sponsors, team members, and end-users.

### 7. Risks and Mitigation Strategies

* **Risks**: A list of potential risks or challenges that could impact the project's success, along with mitigation strategies to address them.

### 8. Timeline

* **Timeline**: A high-level overview of the project's schedule, including key milestones, deadlines, and dependencies.

### 9. Resources

* **Resources**: A list of the resources required to complete the project, including personnel, equipment, and materials.

### 10. Acceptance Criteria

* **Acceptance Criteria**: A clear set of criteria that must be met for each task or deliverable to be considered complete and accepted by stakeholders.

### 11. Labels

* **Labels**: A list of relevant labels that can be applied to the ticket to help with filtering, prioritization, and organization.

### 12. Attachments

* **Attachments**: Any relevant files, documents, or resources that should be associated with the ticket.

### 13. Comments

* **Comments**: A space for team members to provide additional information, ask questions, or share feedback related to the ticket.

### 14. Status

* **Status**: The current status of the ticket (e.g., open, in progress, completed, blocked, etc.).

### 15. Priority

* **Priority**: The relative importance of the ticket compared to other tasks or issues within the project.

### 16. Sub-Tasks

* **Sub-Tasks**: If applicable, a list of sub-tasks or smaller deliverables that need to be completed as part of the main ticket.

### 17. Epic

* **Epic**: If the ticket is part of a larger, ongoing project or initiative, this field should be used to link the ticket to the relevant epic.

### 18. Task Type

* **Task Type**: The type of task being completed (e.g., bug fix, new feature, documentation, etc.).

### 19. Custom Fields

* **Custom Fields**: Any additional custom fields that are relevant to the project and should be included in the ticket.

### 20. Summary

* **Summary**: A concise summary of the ticket, highlighting its key components and objectives.

By using this template, team members can ensure that all critical aspects of the project scope are accurately and completely included in Jira tickets. This will help to facilitate effective issue tracking and management within the Jira system, ultimately leading to a more successful project outcome.

1. User Story: As a user, I want to be able to view the current status of my orders, including their delivery status, so that I can track my shipments and receive updates on their delivery.
Acceptance Criteria:
a. The system should display the current status of all orders placed by the user, including the delivery status, shipping carrier, and estimated delivery date.
b. The system should provide real-time updates on the delivery status of each order, including any changes to the estimated delivery date or carrier information.
c. The system should allow the user to filter and sort orders by various criteria, such as delivery status, order date, or shipping carrier.
d. The system should provide a notification system that alerts the user of any changes to the delivery status or estimated delivery date of their orders.
2. User Story: As a user, I want to be able to view my order history, including the products I have purchased and their corresponding delivery status, so that I can track my past orders and manage my account.
Acceptance Criteria:
a. The system should provide a user-friendly interface that allows the user to view their entire order history, including the products purchased, delivery status, and any relevant notes or comments.
b. The system should allow the user to filter and sort their order history by various criteria, such as order date, product name, or delivery status.
c. The system should provide a search function that allows the user to quickly find specific orders within their order history.
d. The system should provide a way for the user to export their order history in a standard format, such as a CSV file, for further analysis or backup purposes.
3. User Story: As a user, I want to be able to track my orders in real-time, so that I can receive updates on their delivery status and manage my account.
Acceptance Criteria:
a. The system should provide real-time updates on the delivery status of each order, including any changes to the estimated delivery date or carrier information.
b. The system should allow the user to receive notifications about any changes to the delivery status or estimated delivery date of their orders.
c. The system should provide a way for the user to view the current location of their shipments in real-time, using a map or other visual representation.
d. The system should allow the user to manage their shipments, such as changing the delivery address or selecting a different shipping method, directly from the order tracking page.
4. User Story: As a user, I want to be able to view my order history and track my orders in multiple languages, so that I can manage my account in my preferred language.
Acceptance Criteria:
a. The system should provide support for multiple languages, including the ability to view and manage orders in the user's preferred language.
b. The system should provide a way for the user to select their preferred language for viewing orders and tracking shipments.
c. The system should automatically detect the user's preferred language based on their browser settings or other available information.
d. The system should provide accurate translations of all order-related information, including product names, delivery status, and carrier information.
5. User Story: As a user, I want to be able to view my order history and track my orders on multiple devices, so that I can manage my account from any device.
Acceptance Criteria:
a. The system should provide a consistent user experience across all devices, including desktop computers, laptops, tablets, and smartphones.
b. The system should allow the user to log in to their account and view their order history and track their orders from any device.
c. The system should provide a responsive design that adapts to the user's device screen size and resolution.
d. The system should provide a way for the user to synchronize their order history and tracking information across multiple devices, using a secure and reliable data synchronization protocol.

The purpose of this paper is to examine the role of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in the global economy, with a particular focus on its influence on the economic development of member countries. The IMF is an international organization that was established in 1944 with the aim of promoting international monetary cooperation, facilitating the expansion of international trade, and promoting sustainable economic growth and high employment (IMF, 2021). This paper will explore the history of the IMF, its mandate, and its role in the global economy.

1.1 Background

The IMF was established in 1944 as a result of the Bretton Woods Conference, which was held in the United States. The conference was attended by representatives from 44 Allied countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada. The main objective of the conference was to establish a new international economic order that would prevent another global economic crisis like the Great Depression (Mundell, 1961). The IMF was created to provide financial assistance to member countries that were experiencing balance of payments problems, and to promote international monetary cooperation (IMF, 2021).

1.2 The IMF's Mandate

The IMF's mandate is to promote international monetary cooperation, facilitate the expansion of international trade, promote sustainable economic growth, and reduce poverty (IMF, 2021). The IMF achieves its mandate by providing financial assistance to member countries, conducting economic research, and advising member countries on economic policy. The IMF also plays a role in the global economy by providing a framework for international economic cooperation and by promoting the stability of the international monetary system.

1.3 The IMF's Role in the Global Economy

The IMF is an important institution in the global economy, and its role has evolved over time. In the early years of its existence, the IMF provided financial assistance to member countries that were experiencing balance of payments problems. However, in recent years, the IMF has taken on a more active role in promoting economic growth and stability in member countries. The IMF provides financial assistance to member countries through loans, and it also provides technical assistance and advice to member countries on economic policy.

1.4 The IMF's Influence on the Economic Development of Member Countries

The IMF has a significant influence on the economic development of member countries. The IMF provides financial assistance to member countries that are experiencing balance of payments problems, and it also provides technical assistance and advice on economic policy. The IMF's influence on the economic development of member countries is both positive and negative. On the positive side, the IMF provides financial assistance to member countries that are experiencing economic difficulties, which can help to stabilize the economy and promote economic growth. On the negative side, the IMF's conditional lending policies can have a negative impact on the economic development of member countries. The IMF's conditional lending policies often require member countries to implement economic policies that may not be in their best interest, such as reducing government spending and increasing taxes.

1.5 Conclusion

In conclusion, the IMF plays a significant role in the global economy, and its influence on the economic development of member countries is both positive and negative. The IMF provides financial assistance to member countries that are experiencing economic difficulties, and it also provides technical assistance and advice on economic policy. However, the IMF's conditional lending policies can have a negative impact on the economic development of member countries.
